title: adaptive residency entropy reduction and greedy restitch for paged-KV
creator: Mei Chen
description:
Problem: On mixed-tenant workloads we observe persistent tail latency spikes during prefill/decode waves caused by highly fragmented KV residency across slab tiles. Fragmented residency forces the kernel selector to route small noncontiguous fragments to multiple kernel instances, increasing launch overhead and preventing efficient memcpy coalescing. Current eviction heuristics are reactive and can cause oscillation: aggressive compaction during load increases copy cost and stalls, while conservative policies leave many small fragments that amplify decode latency for long prompts.

Goal: Introduce an adaptive, low-cost background mechanism that (1) quantifies KV fragmentation with a Residency Entropy metric, (2) opportunistically performs greedy restitching/coalescence during low-util windows, and (3) integrates residency signals into kernel selection and prefill admission so kernels prefer contiguous ranges and avoid high-fragment handoffs. The approach must be tenant-aware and preserve isolation guarantees for Dedicated workloads.

Design summary:
- Residency Entropy: a lightweight per-shard metric computed from slot occupancy histograms (tile-level) that yields a 0..1 score reflecting spread/fragmentation. Exposed to telemetry and used as a signal (not a hard limit) for restitching and eviction.
- Greedy Restitcher: background daemon that scans candidate fragments and tries to relocate small adjacent fragments into a free slab window using non-blocking copy-on-write relocation. Rate-limited by memory bandwidth and gated by slab pressure and SLO headroom. Restitcher prefers moves that reduce entropy the most per-copy-byte.
- Kernel-affinity hints: extend kernel selection API with an optional contiguous-range hint. Scheduler uses the residency entropy to prefer placing work on kernels with colocated data; if no single kernel covers range, it attempts to pick the fewest kernels possible.
- Prefill admission bias: prefill admission controller will create priority buckets for tokens whose KV ranges are already contiguous locally, enabling low-latency fast-paths. Non-contiguous requests can be admitted at lower priority or batched differently.
- Tenant-aware soft-reservation: implement a soft credit allocator that prevents a single tenant from triggering restitching churn across the entire shard. Credits decay over time.
- Safety: all moves are non-blocking to inflight decodes; relocation uses two-phase install (write new copy, update indirection atomically, schedule old-fragment free) to avoid stalls. Feature behind FF; gated rollout across canary nodes.

Acceptance criteria:
1) Residency Entropy metric included in telemetry and Console (per-shard histogram + trend) documented in PRD.
2) In benchmark mixed workload (50% long prompts, 50% short), 95th percentile prefill latency reduced by >=25% and 99th by >=15% compared to baseline on same hardware.
3) Measured entropy reduction >=30% after restitcher runs in steady-state tests.
4) No regression >5% in median decode latency or steady-state throughput.
5) Unit and integration tests for relocation correctness including concurrent decode interactions.
6) Canary rollout plan with automatic rollback threshold; FF + runtime-1.21 release notes.

Instrumentation/observability:
- New metrics: shard_residency_entropy, restitch_moves_total, restitch_bytes_moved, restitch_backpressure_events, kernel_affinity_hit_rate.
- Dashboard: entropy heatmap, moves over time, correlation with prefill tail latency.

Bench plan: local replay harness + dedicated 4-GPU canary cluster. Initial microbench: synthetic fragmentation patterns (even/clustered/random) to measure copy cost per-byte. End-to-end: production-like tenant mix from telemetry sample A.

Risks and mitigations:
- Copy cost could increase overall throughput under high load. Mitigate by strict rate limiting and backpressure integration with autoscaler.
- Complexity of two-phase install may regress correctness; mitigate with thorough invariants and tests.
- Cross-tenant memory movement could be controversial for Dedicated; use tenant-aware soft-reservation and opt-out flag for strict isolation customers.

comments: 2026-03-01 Mei Chen: Kickoff meeting notes: scoped MVP to one shard-type (x8 slab tiles) and non-tenant-migrations first. Agreed to prototype Residency Entropy and a proof-of-concept restitcher in a feature-flagged background thread. Action: Liam to spike non-blocking relocation design.

2026-03-03 Liam O'Connor: Spike complete: implemented entropy histogram sampler and a naive restitch copy loop. Microbench results: copy cost ~0.9us/KB on canary hardware; restitching 128KB fragments reduces kernel count for those requests from 3->1. Code in branch feat/entropy-restitch-spike. GitHub: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6789

2026-03-05 Carlos Rivera (review): Concern about eviction interplay: moving fragments may increase eviction pressure elsewhere. Suggest adding 'move budget' per shard tied to free_bytes and request_qps. Also flagged potential priority inversion with prefill admission — see comment on PR.

2026-03-07 Mei Chen: Updated design to include soft-reservation credit allocator and bandwidth-rate limiter. Added kernel-affinity hint to scheduler API as an optional opaque struct to avoid breaking existing callers.

2026-03-09 Performance run (synthetic mixed): baseline 95p prefill=78ms, after restitcher 95p prefill=56ms (28% improvement). Entropy metric dropped from 0.62->0.39 after 30 minutes of background restitching. Full run artifacts: https://perf.redwood.ai/runs/PR-entropy-2026-03-09
2026-03-11 Design review (PM + Platform): PM requests UX of entropy to be simplified for Console (0-100 score). Platform asks for canary rollback thresholds (set to 2x baseline 95p latency for now).

2026-03-12 Mei Chen: Implemented two-phase install and atomic indirection update. Added unit tests for concurrent decode + relocation; all green locally. Preparing integration test in canary cluster. GitHub PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/6843

2026-03-13 QA: Integration run in canary cluster shows no median regression; throughput down 3% under heavy batch write workloads (within tolerable limits). Discovered a minor race where restitcher abandoned half-completed moves during shard leadership transfer — added compensation step to detect and finish incomplete moves on new leader.

2026-03-14 Liam O'Connor: Next: finalize Console dashboard, add feature flag/opt-out for Dedicated customers, and draft rollout playbook. Plan to open canary for a subset of production tenants next week pending PM sign-off.
